$comment: OMN-17334. The vocabulary of a git-stash mutation this guard refuses, and
the safe alternative it points a caller at.
Read by plugins/onex/hooks/lib/git_stash_guard.py, which is invoked by the
pre_tool_use_git_stash_guard.sh PreToolUse hook. The vocabulary lives
here, not in the checker, matching the OMN-17957 credential-rotation
policy this guard is patterned on: adding a shape is a config edit
visible in one place rather than a rule a reader has to infer from a
Python literal.
Why this exists
git's stash is ONE repo-wide stack, shared by every worktree of a clone.
A worktree's `.git` is a FILE pointing at the parent clone's git dir, so
`git stash push` / `git stash pop` run inside a worktree operate on the
SAME stash list every other worktree of that clone shares. The push/pop
idiom lanes use to prove a test is RED-without-the-fix is therefore unsafe
by construction: a scoped `git stash push -- <path>` on a tree with no
changes to that path silently creates NO entry and still exits 0, so the
paired `git stash pop` pops whatever is at stash@{0} -- another lane's
work -- and a `git stash pop` can win a race against a peer lane's own
push/pop pair even when the push DID create an entry. Measured six times
by 2026-09-16, in omnibase_infra and omnimarket, twice destroying a peer
lane's uncommitted work outright.
rotation_shapes is named that way for parity with the credential-rotation
policy this file mirrors; here each shape is a git-stash MUTATION rather
than a credential rotation. There is exactly one shape.
mutating_subcommands -- every git-stash subcommand this guard refuses when
the target resolves to a worktree or a canonical clone under $OMNI_HOME:
it writes to, reads destructively from, or otherwise advances the
stash ref. `stash` with NO subcommand is equivalent to `stash push` and
is refused on the same terms -- the checker treats a bare invocation as
the `push` shape.
safe_subcommands -- `list` and `show` are read-only against the stash ref
and are never gated. They are not allowlisted as an exception; they
simply never match the mutating shape.
safe_alternative -- the replacement that never touches the shared stash
stack. It leads with the object-store read because the path-scoped
checkout pair recorded by the lane that hit the sixth occurrence
discards uncommitted work whenever HEAD is still the base -- four lanes
lost work that way (OMN-18874), and the shared-tree guard now refuses
that pair over a dirty path.
worktree_root_env / worktree_root_env_legacy -- the same override pair
pre_tool_use_worktree_guard.sh (OMN-14330) resolves against, so this
guard's notion of "under $OMNI_HOME" agrees with the worktree guard's.
There is deliberately NO escape entry -- no wildcard shape, no exempt
marker. A lane that genuinely needs the shared stash (a non-worktree,
a clone not under $OMNI_HOME) is already outside every condition this
guard checks, which is where the read/list case lives too.
safe_alternative: read the pre-image without touching the tree with git show origin/dev:<path> > <scratch file>; or commit your work first (confirm with git log -1), then git checkout origin/dev -- <path> and restore it with git checkout HEAD -- <path>, scoped to named paths
